label_policy: Adequate means the supplied text reports an observed relation answering the question. An observed null effect qualifies; unperformed experiments and hypotheses do not. Labels are authored development expectations, not independently reviewed scientific gold.

cases.question: How does mixture composition affect conductivity?
texts: We measured conductivity in the mixture at varying compositions. Conductivity increased as the fraction of component A increased.

cases.question: How does mixture composition affect conductivity?
texts: We did not measure how mixture composition affects conductivity at varying compositions. No composition-dependent conductivity measurements were performed.
cases.rationale: Explicitly says the relevant measurement was not performed.

cases.question: How does mixture composition affect conductivity?
texts: We hypothesize that mixture composition affects conductivity: conductivity may increase as the fraction increases. This hypothesis has not been tested.
cases.rationale: Untested hypothesis cannot establish the experimental dependence.

cases.question: How does mixture composition affect conductivity?
texts: We measured conductivity in the mixture at varying compositions. Mixture composition did not affect conductivity within measurement uncertainty.
cases.rationale: A measured null effect is relevant evidence, despite negation.

cases.question: How does mixing temperature affect swelling during heating and cooling?
texts: We measured swelling during heating and cooling. Raising the mixing temperature increased swelling in both cycles.
cases.rationale: Reports measurements linking the requested condition and response.

cases.question: How does mixing temperature affect swelling during heating and cooling?
texts: The effect of mixing temperature on swelling during heating and cooling was not investigated. No such experiments were performed.
cases.rationale: All cues occur in an explicit statement of missing measurements.

cases.question: How does mixing temperature affect swelling during heating and cooling?
texts: Mixing temperature was recorded for preparation of sample A. Swelling was measured in an unrelated sample B at room temperature. Heating and cooling were used only to calibrate an empty instrument.
cases.rationale: Cue co-occurrence spans unrelated experiments within one fragment.

cases.question: Как температура смешения влияет на набухание при нагреве и охлаждении?
texts: Влияние температуры смешения на набухание при нагреве и охлаждении не исследовали. Такие измерения не проводились.
cases.rationale: Russian explicit absence of the requested measurements.

cases.question: How does mixing temperature affect swelling during heating and cooling?
texts: Samples blended at higher temperatures absorbed more solvent, both when warmed and when subsequently chilled. This dependence was measured in repeated experiments.
cases.rationale: Experimental relation expressed without the exact cue vocabulary.

cases.question: How does mixing temperature affect swelling during heating and cooling?
texts: Mixing temperature affects swelling in sample A.
Heating and cooling were used to calibrate a separate instrument.
cases.rationale: Negative control: unrelated fragments must not supply joint experimental context.
